Want to experience the nano-texture feel of an iPad screen, but don't want to commit long-term? Astropad has launched a brand new version of its Rock Paper Pencil product, retaining the detachable design while adding a second writing texture.

Graphite feel officially arrives on Apple Pencil and iPad, thanks to Rock Paper Pencil 4.0

Rock Paper Pencil 4.0 pairs a screen protector with nano-texture together with a specialised Apple Pencil tip. For the first time, users can freely choose between the smooth feel of a ballpoint pen and the softer, rougher resistance of graphite.

The brand new graphite tip is specifically designed to mimic a 2B pencil, even replicating the feel that artists love when drawing, shading sketches and expressing strokes.

Astropad stated that developing this new option took approximately one year, using a standard 2B pencil as the reference benchmark. The company also noted that the finished product reproduces both the visual effect and writing sound of real graphite.

Choose between ballpoint or standard pencil feel

Meanwhile, the existing steel ballpoint tip remains on sale, suitable for writing, inking, precise line drawing and neat note-taking. Each Rock Paper Pencil 4.0 set now comes with a total of four Apple Pencil tips, including two ballpoint tips and two graphite tips.

The screen protector itself has not been changed. Astropad's proprietary NanoCling system uses electrostatic adhesion instead of adhesives, allowing the protector to be applied, peeled off and reused repeatedly without leaving any residue.

The company says the fit is more secure than magnetism, while also supporting bubble-free installation and easy removal. The microscopic texture on the protector mimics the roughness of fine-grain paper, providing friction and enhancing control.

The best matte screen protector for iPad

Rock Paper Pencil 4.0 is not just a standalone improvement to the Apple Pencil tip or screen texture, but treats the two as an integrated system. Astropad notes that the specialised tip only works with the nano-texture protector. The new graphite tip is made of POM plastic, while the ballpoint version uses steel.

Rock Paper Pencil 4.0 is now officially on sale, priced at US$49.99, with worldwide shipping available. The 3.0 version is also undergoing clearance discounts, available while stocks last.
